<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par74 />{{GHGpar-heading|74|Verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״א}}, ''e.g.'' {{GHGheb|text=מָצָא}} to find. Paradigm O}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|a}}
The {{GHGheb|text=א}} in these verbs, as in verbs {{GHGheb|text=פ״א}}, is treated in some cases as a consonant, i.e. as a guttural, in others as having no consonantal value (as a quiescent or vowel letter), viz.:

'''1.''' In those forms which terminate with the {{GHGheb|text=א}}, the final syllable always has the regular vowels, if long, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מֹצֵא}}, {{GHGheb|text=מִצֵּא}}, {{GHGheb|text=מָצוּא}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִמְצִיא}}, i.e. the {{GHGheb|text=א}} simply quiesces in the long vowel, without the latter suffering any change whatever. It is just possible that after the altogether heterogeneous vowel ''û'' the {{GHGheb|text=א}} may originally have preserved a certain consonantal value. On the other hand, if the final {{GHGheb|text=א}} quiesces in a preceding ''ă'' (as in the ''perfect, imperfect'', and {{GHGterm|imperative Qal}}, in the {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}}, and in {{GHGterm|Puʿal}} and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}) this ''ă'' is necessarily lengthened to ''ā'', by {{GHGpar|27|g}}, as standing in an open syllable; e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מָצָא}}, {{GHGheb|text=יִמְצָא}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|b}}
The {{GHGterm|imperfect}} and {{GHGterm|imperative Qal}} invariably have ''ā'' in the final syllable, on the analogy of verbs ''tertiae gutturalis''; cf., however, {{GHGpar|76|e}}.—In the ''imperfect Hithpaʿēl ā'' occurs in the final syllable not only (according to {{GHGpar|54|k}}) in the principal pause ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=31|verse=23}}), or immediately before it ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=10|verse=16}}), or with the lesser disjunctives ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=21|verse=1.4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=19|verse=13.20}}), but even out of pause with ''Mer<sup>e</sup>kha'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=6|verse=7}}, and even before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=19|verse=12}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|c}}
'''2.''' When {{GHGheb|text=א}} stands at the end of a syllable before an afformative beginning with a consonant ({{GHGheb|text=ת}}, {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}}), it likewise quiesces with the preceding vowel; thus in the {{GHGterm|perfect Qal}} (and {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}}, see below) quiescing with ''ă'' it regularly becomes ''Qameṣ'' ({{GHGheb|text=מָצָ֫אתָ}} for {{GHGheb|text=מָצַ֫אְתָּ}}, &c.); but in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} of all the other active and reflexive conjugations, so far as they occur, it is preceded by ''Ṣere'' ({{GHGheb|text=נִמְצֵ֫אתָ}}, &c.), and in the {{GHGterm|imperative}} and {{GHGterm|imperfect}} by {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}}, {{GHGheb|text=מְצֶ֫אנָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=תִּמְצֶאנָה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|d}}
(''a'') The {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} of these forms of the imperfect and imperative might be considered as a modification, and at the same time a lengthening of an original ''ă'' (see {{GHGpar|8|a}}). In the same way the ''ē'' of the {{GHGterm|perfect}} forms in ''Piʿēl, Hithpaʿēl'', and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} might be traced to an original ''ĭ'' (as in other cases the ''ē'' and ''î'' in the final syllable of the 3rd ''sing. masc. perfect'' of these conjugations), although this ''ĭ'' may have only been attenuated from an original ''ă''. According to another, and probably the correct explanation, however, both the {{GHGterm|Ṣere}} and the {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} are due to the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} ({{GHGpar|75|f}}) in consequence of the close relation between the two classes, cf. {{GHGpar|75|nn}}.—No form of this kind occurs in {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}; in the {{GHGterm|perfect Hophʿal}} only the 2nd ''masc. sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=הֻבָ֫אתָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=40|verse=4}}, lengthened according to rule.

{{GHGmargin-letter|74|e}}
(''b'') Before suffixes attached by a connecting vowel (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרָאֵ֫נִי}}) the {{GHGheb|text=א}} retains its consonantal value; so before {{GHGheb|text=ךָ}} and {{GHGheb|text=כֶם}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֶמְצָֽאֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=8|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=הִבָּרַֽאֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=28|verse=13}} (cf. {{GHGpar|65|h}}), not {{GHGheb|text=אֶמְצָאךָ}}, &c., since these suffixes, by {{GHGpar|58|f}}, are likewise attached to the verb-form by a connecting vowel in the form of {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ mobile}}.—As {{GHGterm|infinitive Qal}} with suffix notice {{GHGheb|text=מַחְאֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=25|verse=6}}; {{GHGterm|participle}} with suffix {{GHGheb|text=בֹּרַֽאֲךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=43|verse=1}}; {{GHGterm|infinitive Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּטַמַּֽאֲכֶם}}.—The doubly anomalous form {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרְאוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=6}} (for {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרָאֵ֫הוּ}} or {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרָאֶ֫נּוּ}}) is perhaps a ''forma mixta'' combining the readings {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרָאוֹ}} and {{GHGheb|text=יִקְרְאוּ}}.
